about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Pandesal Filipino Rolls
recipes.summary: Soft, lightly sweet Filipino bread rolls rolled in breadcrumbs, best eaten warm.
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then stir in the milk, egg and butter to form a dough. Knead for 8 minutes on a floured bench until smooth and elastic, then cover and leave until doubled.
Roll the dough into a log and cut into 12 even pieces. Roll each piece in the breadcrumbs and place cut side up on a lined tray, 3cm apart. Cover and rest until puffy.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Bake for 18 minutes, until golden and the bases sound hollow when tapped.
Cool on a rack for 10 minutes before serving warm.
notes: Snack. Allow about 1 hour 30 minutes of proving, not included in the times. Per serving: 1 roll. Keeps 2 days in a sealed bag; freeze for up to 2 months and reheat at 160°C fan for 6 minutes.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, wash your hands after handling raw egg, and bake the rolls until cooked through. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Steamed Bao Buns with Hoisin Mushrooms
recipes.summary: Pillowy steamed buns folded around quick hoisin mushrooms and spring onion.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and baking powder, add the water and oil, and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave until doubled.
Roll the dough into 8 balls, flatten each into an oval about 10cm long, brush lightly with oil and fold in half over a small square of baking paper. Rest until puffy.
Fry the mushrooms in a dry non-stick frying pan over high heat for 6 minutes until golden and the liquid has gone, then stir in the hoisin and soy sauce for 1 minute.
Steam the buns in a lined steamer over simmering water for 12 minutes, until puffed and springy to the touch. Fill with the mushrooms and spring onions.
notes: Snack. Allow about 1 hour 20 minutes of proving, not included in the times. Per serving: 1 filled bun. Unfilled buns keep 3 days in the fridge or freeze for 2 months; re-steam for 5 minutes. Check the hoisin label if you need it gluten free.

recipes.title: Cheesy Naan Bites
recipes.summary: Quick yoghurt naan stuffed with mozzarella and brushed with garlic butter, no yeast needed.
steps: Mix the flour, yoghurt and oil into a soft dough and knead for 2 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes, then divide into 8 balls.
Flatten each ball into a 10cm round, put a spoonful of mozzarella in the centre, pinch to seal and roll out to 12cm.
Cook each naan in a hot dry frying pan for 2 minutes per side, until puffed and spotted brown.
Stir the garlic into the melted butter, brush over the naan and scatter with coriander. Cut each into 3 wedges.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 naan. Best warm; keeps 2 days in the fridge, reheat in a dry pan for 1 minute per side.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Sesame Bagel Bites
recipes.summary: Mini bagels boiled in honey water then baked with a sesame crust.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, add the water and 1 tbsp of the honey and knead for 10 minutes into a firm, smooth dough. Cover and leave until doubled.
Divide into 12 pieces, roll each into a ball and poke a hole through the centre, stretching to 3cm wide. Rest on a floured tray until puffy.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Bring a wide pan of water with the remaining honey to a gentle boil and simmer the bagels in batches for 1 minute each side. Drain on a rack.
Brush with the egg white, dip the tops in the sesame seeds and bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes, until deep golden.
notes: Snack. Allow about 1 hour 15 minutes of proving, not included in the times. Per serving: 1 mini bagel. Keeps 2 days in a paper bag; freeze for 2 months and toast from frozen.
Food safety: wash your hands after handling raw egg white, and bake the bagels until fully cooked through.

recipes.title: Garlic Flatbread Wedges
recipes.summary: Soft yoghurt flatbreads brushed with garlic butter and parsley, cut into wedges for dipping.
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and yoghurt into a soft dough, knead for 1 minute and divide into 8 balls.
Roll each ball into a 15cm round. Cook in a hot dry frying pan for 90 seconds per side, until puffed with brown spots.
Mix the butter, garlic and parsley and brush over the hot flatbreads. Cut each into 4 wedges.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 flatbread (4 wedges). Keeps 2 days in a sealed bag; reheat in a dry pan.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Sourdough Discard Crackers
recipes.summary: Crisp rosemary and sesame crackers that use up spare sourdough starter.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the starter, flour, oil, salt, sesame seeds and rosemary into a firm dough.
Roll the dough between 2 sheets of baking paper to 2mm thick, slide onto a tray, sprinkle with flaky salt and cut into 5cm squares with a knife or pizza cutter.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden and crisp, turning the tray halfway. Cool on the tray.
notes: Snack. Per serving: about 6 crackers. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container. If they soften, re-crisp at 150°C fan for 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Soft Milk Bread Rolls
recipes.summary: Fluffy Japanese-style rolls made with a cooked flour paste that keeps them soft for days.

items: 30g bread flour, extra, for the paste

steps: Whisk the extra flour with 100ml of the milk and 50ml water in a small pan over medium heat for 2 minutes, until it forms a thick paste. Cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the paste, remaining milk, egg and butter. Knead for 12 minutes until smooth and stretchy. Cover and leave until doubled.
Divide into 12 balls and place in a lined 20 x 30cm tin. Cover and rest until puffy. Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional).
Brush with a little milk and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and the centre rolls sound hollow when tapped. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.
notes: Snack. Allow about 1 hour 40 minutes of proving, not included in the times. Per serving: 1 roll. Keeps 3 days in a sealed bag; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, wash your hands after handling raw egg, and bake the rolls until cooked through.

recipes.title: Corn Kernel Cornbread Muffins
recipes.summary: Golden cornmeal muffins studded with sweet corn, good warm with butter.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C fan (210°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the flour, polenta, baking powder, sugar and salt in a bowl. Whisk the egg, milk and butter, pour into the dry mix with the corn and stir until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake the muffins until a skewer comes out clean.

recipes.title: Sticky Raisin Toffee Pudding
recipes.summary: A soft, moist raisin sponge soaked in hot toffee sauce, the sticky date idea without dates.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and grease and line a 20cm square tin. Soak the raisins in the boiling water with the bicarbonate of soda for 10 minutes.
Beat the butter and first measure of sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour, then the raisins and their liquid. Pour into the tin.
Bake for 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Meanwhile simmer the sauce ingredients in a small pan for 4 minutes, stirring, until smooth and glossy.
Cut the pudding into 8 squares and serve warm with the sauce spooned over.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square with sauce. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat in the microwave for 40 seconds.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until a skewer comes out clean, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Creamy Rice Pudding Cups
recipes.summary: Slow-simmered vanilla rice pudding with a cinnamon dusting, served warm or cold.
steps: Put the rice, milk and sugar in a heavy saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring, until the sugar dissolves.
Cook over low heat for 45 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the rice is tender and the pudding is thick and creamy.
Stir in the vanilla, spoon into 8 small cups and dust with cinnamon.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 small cup. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; loosen with a splash of milk. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking.

recipes.title: Vegetarian Coconut Pudding Cups with Mango
recipes.summary: Cornflour-set vanilla coconut puddings topped with fresh mango, no gelatine.
steps: Whisk the cornflour with 100ml of the almond milk until smooth. Heat the coconut milk, remaining almond milk and sugar in a saucepan until steaming.
Whisk in the cornflour mix and cook over medium heat for 4 minutes, stirring, until thick and bubbling. Stir in the vanilla.
Pour into 6 cups and cool for 15 minutes, then chill until set. Toss the mango with the lime juice and spoon over to serve.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 cup. Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.

recipes.title: Crema Caramel Flan
recipes.summary: A silky baked custard turned out over a pool of golden caramel.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Melt the caramel sugar in a small pan over medium heat, without stirring, for 6 minutes until amber. Pour into a 20cm round cake tin or flan dish and tilt to coat the base.
Whisk the eggs, yolks, remaining sugar and vanilla. Warm the milk until steaming, whisk it into the eggs, then strain over the caramel.
Set the tin in a roasting tray, pour in hot water to halfway up the sides and bake for 45 minutes, until the edge is set and the centre has a slight wobble.
Cool, chill, then run a knife around the edge and turn out onto a plate. Cut into 8 wedges.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 wedge. Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until the custard is set, and refrigerate within 2 hours. Not for anyone who needs to avoid lightly set egg.

recipes.title: Halo-Halo-Style Fruit Ice Cups
recipes.summary: Crushed ice layered with mango, pineapple and milk, a no-cook take on the Filipino classic.
steps: Crush the ice in a blender or in a clean tea towel with a rolling pin until fine and snowy.
Layer the mango and pineapple into 6 tall glasses, then pile on the crushed ice.
Stir the evaporated and condensed milk, pour over the ice and top with corn flakes. Serve straight away with a long spoon and mix before eating.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 glass. Make just before serving; the ice melts fast. Use ice from clean water.

recipes.title: Baked Vanilla Custard Cups
recipes.summary: Gently baked egg custards with a nutmeg top, set in small cups.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Whisk the eggs, yolks, sugar and vanilla. Warm the milk and cream until steaming, then whisk into the eggs and strain.
Pour into 6 ovenproof cups, dust with nutmeg and stand in a deep tray. Pour in hot water to halfway up the cups.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the custards are set at the edge with a slight wobble in the centre. Cool, then chill.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 cup. Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until set, and refrigerate within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Berry Swirl Yoghurt Pops
recipes.summary: Blended frozen berries and yoghurt, sweetened with a little honey.
steps: Blend the berries, yoghurt, honey and orange juice until smooth.
Pour into 8 ice block moulds, add sticks and freeze for at least 5 hours, until solid.
Run the moulds under warm water for 10 seconds to release.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 ice block. Keeps 2 months in the freezer. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

recipes.title: Pistachio Kulfi
recipes.summary: Dense, creamy Indian ice cream flavoured with pistachios and rosewater.
steps: Simmer the evaporated and condensed milk in a saucepan for 10 minutes over low heat, stirring, until slightly thickened. Cool completely.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, fold in the cooled milk, chopped pistachios and rosewater.
Spoon into 8 small moulds or cups, cover and freeze for at least 6 hours, until firm.
Dip the moulds briefly in warm water to release, and top with a whole pistachio.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 kulfi. Keeps 1 month in the freezer. Contains tree nuts. Refrigerate the cooled milk if you are not folding it in right away.

recipes.title: Watermelon Granita
recipes.summary: Icy, fluffy shards of watermelon and lime, scraped with a fork.
steps: Blend the watermelon, sugar and lime juice until smooth, then pour into a shallow metal tray.
Freeze until ice forms around the edges, then scrape with a fork. Repeat 3 or 4 more times, until the whole tray is a mass of fine, fluffy ice crystals.
Spoon into 8 chilled glasses and serve straight away.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 glass. Keeps 1 week in the freezer; rake with a fork before serving.

recipes.title: Honey Pistachio Yoghurt Shards
recipes.summary: Thin sheets of honey yoghurt frozen with berries and pistachios, snapped into shards.
steps: Line a 25 x 35cm tray with baking paper. Mix the yoghurt and honey and spread to 8mm thick.
Scatter with the berries and pistachios, pressing them in lightly. Freeze for at least 3 hours, until completely firm.
Break into 12 shards and serve straight from the freezer.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 shard. Keeps 1 month in an airtight container in the freezer. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey. Contains tree nuts.

recipes.title: Mango Nice Cream
recipes.summary: Frozen mango blended with yoghurt into a soft-serve texture, no ice-cream machine needed.
steps: Let the mango sit at room temperature for 5 minutes. Blend with the yoghurt, honey and lime juice, scraping down the sides, until smooth and thick.
Serve straight away in 4 bowls as soft-serve.
For a scoopable texture, spoon into a container and freeze until firm enough to scoop.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bowl. Best the day it is made. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

recipes.title: Lemon Sorbet Cups
recipes.summary: A sharp, clean lemon sorbet churned by hand in the freezer.
steps: Heat the sugar and water in a small pan for 3 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves. Cool completely, then stir in the lemon juice and zest.
Pour into a shallow container and freeze until slushy at the edges. Beat well with a fork, then repeat 3 or 4 more times, until smooth and scoopable.
Scoop into 8 small cups to serve.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 small cup. Keeps 1 month in the freezer; soften for 10 minutes before scooping.

recipes.title: Chocolate Fudge Ice Blocks
recipes.summary: Thick chocolate milk custard frozen into old-school ice blocks.
steps: Whisk the cocoa, sugar and cornflour in a saucepan, then whisk in a splash of the milk to make a paste. Add the remaining milk.
Heat over medium heat for 6 minutes, stirring, until the mixture bubbles and thickens. Stir in the vanilla and cool.
Pour into 8 moulds, add sticks and freeze for at least 5 hours until solid.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 ice block. Keeps 2 months in the freezer.

recipes.title: Pineapple Coconut Ice Blocks
recipes.summary: Blended pineapple and coconut milk with a squeeze of lime, a tropical ice block.
steps: Blend the pineapple, coconut milk, sugar and lime juice until smooth.
Pour into 8 moulds, add sticks and freeze for at least 5 hours, until solid.
Run the moulds under warm water for 10 seconds to release.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 ice block. Keeps 2 months in the freezer.

recipes.title: Sutlac Turkish Baked Rice Pudding
recipes.summary: Rice pudding simmered then baked until the top blisters golden-brown.
steps: Simmer the rice in 250ml water for 10 minutes until the water is absorbed. Add 700ml of the milk and the sugar and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Mix the cornflour with the remaining milk, stir it in and cook for 3 minutes until thickened. Stir in the vanilla.

Heat the grill to high. Divide among 6 ovenproof bowls and grill 10cm from the heat for 5 minutes, until the tops blister and brown. Alternatively bake at 220°C fan (240°C conventional) for 12 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes and serve warm, or chill.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bowl. Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking.

recipes.title: Bread and Butter Pudding Squares
recipes.summary: Buttered bread layered with sultanas and baked in a soft vanilla custard.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and grease a 20cm square dish. Butter the bread, cut into triangles and layer in the dish with the sultanas.
Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar and vanilla and pour over the bread. Leave to soak for 10 minutes.
Bake for 40 minutes, until golden on top and the custard is just set in the centre. Cool for 10 minutes and cut into 8 squares.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat in the microwave for 40 seconds.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until the custard is set, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.
